copy_prompt: Each [morning], check stock in [system] against minimums [file], open orders or jobs against the stock or parts they need, and order tracking for anything with no update in [5] days. List problems with a suggested next step for each. Draft customer messages where needed. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Problems surface while there is still time to fix them quietly.

title: Tracking supplier lead times and late deliveries
summary: SI records when you place and receive orders. It works out each supplier's real lead time. It flags late deliveries early.
problem: Lead times are guesses. They come from what a supplier once said. Late deliveries show up only when something is missing. Planning uses numbers nobody has checked.
what_si_does: SI logs order dates, promised dates, and received dates. It reads purchase orders, confirmations, and receiving records. It works out each supplier's usual lead time. It also works out the on-time rate from recent orders. It flags open orders past their promised date. It drafts a polite chase email.
setup: Purchase order and receiving records, plus supplier emails. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A person approves chase emails before sending.
The owner decides any supplier changes.
A person reviews lead-time figures before they feed reorder planning.

examples.scenario: Hardware from one supplier now takes about twice as long as quoted. The reorder plan is updated.
Nursery orders for a spring planting job are past their promised date. SI drafts a chase email to the nursery.
SI tracks can and label deliveries. Production dates are set around real lead times.

copy_prompt: From these purchase orders and receiving records [files], calculate each supplier's typical lead time and share of on-time deliveries over the last [6] months. List open orders past their promised date and draft a polite chase email for each. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Planning uses real lead times. Late deliveries get chased before they cause problems.

title: Inventory value and aging report
summary: SI shows how much money sits in stock. It shows what has not moved in months. It suggests what to discount, return, or stop buying.
problem: Cash gets tied up in items that sit on shelves. Without an aging view, slow items keep getting reordered. Dead stock shows up at year-end counts.
what_si_does: SI combines stock on hand, unit cost, and last sale or use date. It shows inventory value by category and age band. Bands can be last 30 days, 31 to 90, over 90, or never. It lists the largest pockets of slow stock. Options include return to supplier, discount, bundle, or stop reordering.
setup: Stock, cost and sales or usage data. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: The owner decides what to discount or return.
Cost data is checked against supplier invoices.
Seasonal items are marked so they are not flagged out of season.

examples.scenario: Older-model accessories and a few last-season bikes hold a large share of stock value. The report suggests a fall clearance. It also suggests returning one unopened case.
Fittings for a discontinued fixture line have not moved in a year. They are listed for return or write-off review.
Variants in uncommon sizes have not sold in over 90 days. The report suggests stopping reorders on them.

copy_prompt: Using stock on hand [file], unit costs [file] and last sale or use dates [file], show inventory value by [category] and age band: [0-30, 31-90, 91-180, 180+ days, never]. List the [20] largest slow items with options: return, discount, bundle or stop reordering. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: You see where cash is sitting. You make better calls on what not to reorder.

title: Checking customer orders against their PO and payment
summary: SI checks the paperwork before an order ships or work starts. It compares the customer's purchase order, your invoice, and their payment. It flags any mismatch.
problem: Business customers send purchase orders. Then they pay by transfer with a reference. That reference may or may not match. Mismatched quantities, prices, and amounts cause billing disputes. They also cause delays.
what_si_does: SI reads the customer's purchase order. It reads your sales order or invoice. It reads the payment record or remittance. It checks customer, quantities, prices, totals, tax, and payment amount. It lists mismatches. When everything matches, it drafts the order confirmation. When it does not, it drafts a clarifying question.
setup: Access to the inbox where purchase orders and remittances arrive. You also need invoices and bank or payment records. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A person releases the order or work after reviewing any mismatch.
A person approves confirmation and clarification emails before sending.
Payment records are read-only for SI.

examples.scenario: A school district's purchase order lists a lower unit price than the invoice. The order is held. A clarification is drafted.
A restaurant group's payment covers two of three invoices. The remittance is matched. The gap is noted.
A corporate client's purchase order is matched to the quote and deposit. Then the delivery is scheduled.

copy_prompt: For each order in [inbox/folder], compare the customer's purchase order with our invoice [file] and payment record [file]. Check customer, quantities, prices, totals, tax and amount paid. List mismatches. Draft a confirmation for matches and a clarifying question for mismatches. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Billing disputes are caught before the order ships. They are not found after the invoice is overdue.

title: Product and service descriptions from specs, plus catalog cleanup
summary: SI writes matching descriptions from spec sheets and notes. It cleans names, categories, and details. This covers your catalog, menu, or service list.
problem: Descriptions are missing. Some are copied from suppliers. Some are written in five different styles. Names and categories do not match. That makes things hard to find and harder to sell.
what_si_does: SI reads spec sheets, supplier data, or your own notes. It writes descriptions in one format and voice. Each one says what it is, who it is for, key details, and care or usage notes. It also proposes fixes across the list. Fixes include matching names, missing sizes or details, duplicate entries, and wrong categories. These come as a change sheet for review.
setup: An export of the catalog, menu, or service list. You also need spec sheets and a style example. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A person approves changes before they are applied.
Specs that SI could not confirm are flagged rather than guessed.
Health, safety, and performance claims are checked against the source.

examples.scenario: Stone, mulch, and soil products get descriptions. They include coverage per cubic yard and delivery notes. Duplicate listings for the same gravel are merged.
Service descriptions are rewritten in the same style. They include duration, preparation, and aftercare. They do not make medical claims.
Product titles are set to brand, product, size, and color. Missing material details are listed for the owner to fill in.

copy_prompt: Using these spec sheets [files] and this style example [paste], write descriptions for these items [list] with what it is, who it is for, key details and care or usage notes. Then review this catalog export [file] and propose fixes for naming, missing details, duplicates and categories as a change sheet. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: You get a cleaner catalog in one style. Customers can search it. Staff can keep it up.

title: A newsletter drafted from what actually happened
summary: Each week or month, SI collects real updates. It uses your calendar, projects, photos, and notes. It drafts a newsletter for you to edit.
problem: Newsletters stall because nobody knows what to write. When one does go out, it is vague and late.
what_si_does: SI gathers what actually happened. That includes finished projects, new staff, and upcoming events. It can include new services, a seasonal tip, and customer questions worth answering. It drafts a short issue in your voice. It adds suggested subject lines and photo spots. It leaves out anything not confirmed.
setup: Access to sources such as the calendar or project tool. You can also use a shared photo folder or a notes doc. You also need a couple of past issues. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: The owner edits and approves the issue before it is scheduled.
Customer names or photos are used only with permission.
Mailing lists follow opt-in and unsubscribe rules.

examples.scenario: The monthly issue covers two finished homes with photos. It adds a framing update on a new street. It reminds readers about the warranty-check schedule.
The issue has a seasonal note on ticks. It introduces a new vet. It lists holiday hours.
The issue lists audition dates. It includes a rehearsal photo. It notes volunteer needs for the next show.

copy_prompt: Collect updates for [period] from [calendar, project tool, photo folder, notes doc]. Draft a newsletter in this voice [past issue] with [3-5] short sections, [3] subject-line options and spots for photos. Leave out anything not confirmed in the sources. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Newsletters go out more often. They reflect the real business.

title: A month of social posts from one source
summary: SI turns one source into a month of posts. The source can be updates, photos, or a single article. Each post fits the platform. You approve and schedule them.
problem: Posting regularly is hard to keep up with. Accounts go quiet for weeks. Then they get a burst of rushed posts.
what_si_does: SI drafts a calendar of posts from a source you provide. That source can be a photo folder, a blog post, notes on upcoming events, or past customer questions. Posts are suited to each platform. Each post has captions and posting dates. It adds hashtags where useful and suggested images. It varies the mix. The mix includes work examples, tips, behind-the-scenes, events, and offers.
setup: Access to the source material and the scheduling tool. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: Every post is approved before scheduling.
Photos of people are used only with permission.
The owner checks offers and prices.

examples.scenario: Before-and-after photos of five bathrooms become a month of posts. Short notes cover materials and layout choices.
The weekly specials list and holiday pre-order dates become posts. They are timed to order cutoffs.
A quarterly market letter becomes several short teaching posts. They are reviewed for compliance.

copy_prompt: Using [source: photos, article, notes], draft [12] posts for [platforms] over [month], with captions, suggested image and date for each. Mix work examples, tips, behind-the-scenes and events. Keep my voice [examples]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: You get a steady posting rhythm. You skip the weekly scramble.
caution: Regulated professions usually have rules for public communications. That includes financial, legal, and medical work. Route posts through whoever handles compliance.

title: One talk, class or article into several pieces
summary: SI turns one long piece into shorter pieces. The source can be a talk, webinar, interview, or article. Outputs include posts, an email, a handout, and short video scripts.
problem: Good long content gets used once. Making shorter versions for other channels takes a long time. It can take as long as writing the original.
what_si_does: SI starts from a recording or transcript. It pulls out the strongest points. It drafts several pieces. These include a summary article, an email, and a few short social posts. They also include a one-page handout and short video scripts with suggested clip timestamps. Each piece keeps your wording where possible. Each piece notes its source.
setup: The source recording or document and a style example. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: The speaker or author approves each piece.
Quotes are checked against the transcript.
Nothing is published without approval.

examples.scenario: A webinar on new leave rules becomes several pieces. These include a client alert, an email, three short posts, and a one-page summary for HR managers. An attorney reviews all of them.
A long podcast episode becomes short exercise tips. It also becomes a handout for clients.
The director's annual meeting speech becomes a donor letter. It also becomes a series of impact posts.

copy_prompt: Here is a transcript of [talk/article]: [file]. Draft a summary article, an email, [5] social posts, a one-page handout and [3] short video scripts with timestamps for clips. Keep my wording where possible. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: You get more value from each piece of content. You spend less time rewriting it.

title: Refreshing tired web pages and search snippets
summary: SI reviews your key web pages. It looks for old details, weak titles, and missing information. It proposes specific rewrites you approve.
problem: Service and category pages were written years ago. Hours, prices, and services are out of date. Titles and descriptions in search results are vague. Important questions are not answered.
what_si_does: SI reads your main pages. It checks for outdated details. It checks for missing basics such as service area, hours, and how to book. It checks unclear headings and weak page titles and meta descriptions. It proposes rewrites for each page in a change sheet. It drafts a few short articles that answer common customer questions.
setup: A list of pages. You need the site editor or a person to apply changes. You also need the current facts. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: The owner approves every change.
SI does not change live pages without approval.
The owner confirms facts like prices and services.

examples.scenario: Service pages get clear titles. Titles name the services and towns covered. A new page answers how often chimneys should be inspected.
Practice-area pages are rewritten in plainer language. They include a clear consultation process. An attorney reviews them.
Seasonal category pages are refreshed. They include current plant availability and planting tips.

copy_prompt: Review these pages [URLs]. For each, list outdated details, missing basics [service area, hours, booking], and weak headings. Propose a new page title, meta description and rewritten sections in a change sheet. Suggest [3] short articles answering common questions [list]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: The website is current and clearer. That helps both visitors and search results.

title: Checking marketing copy for claims you cannot back up
summary: SI checks marketing copy before it is published. It checks the copy against your evidence. It flags claims that are not backed up, outdated, or risky.
problem: Marketing copy picks up phrases like 'best in town', 'guaranteed', or 'clinically proven'. Nobody can support those phrases. Old claims stay on the site long after they stopped being true.
what_si_does: SI reads the draft or existing pages. It lists each factual claim. That includes words like best, guarantees, numbers, certifications, results, and comparisons. For each claim it looks for support in the evidence you provide. Evidence can be licenses, certifications, warranty terms, or written results. It labels each claim supported, unsupported, or needs review. It also gives a softer alternative.
setup: The copy to check and a folder of supporting documents. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: The owner or compliance reviewer decides final wording.
SI does not give legal opinions on advertising rules.
The responsible person checks industry-specific rules.

examples.scenario: 'Lifetime warranty' is flagged. The manufacturer warranty has conditions. A clearer phrasing is suggested.
Health benefit claims on product pages are listed for review. They are checked against what is allowed.
A brochure line about 'guaranteed savings' is flagged. It is rewritten.

copy_prompt: Review this copy [draft or URLs]. List every factual claim, guarantee, comparison, number or certification. Check each against this evidence [folder] and label it supported, unsupported or needs review. Suggest a supported alternative for each problem claim. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer claims you cannot stand behind. A cleaner review process before publishing.
caution: Advertising rules vary by industry and place. Health, finance, and legal services are stricter. SI flags wording. It does not replace review by a lawyer or compliance person.

title: Reviewing and rewriting emails your systems send
summary: SI reviews the emails your systems send on their own. These include welcomes, booking confirmations, and follow-ups. It drafts clearer replacements.
problem: These emails were set up once and forgotten. Some have old details. Some are missing entirely. The tone does not match the business.
what_si_does: SI collects your system emails. These include welcome, confirmation, and reminder notes. They also include post-visit or post-purchase notes, review requests, and inactive-customer follow-up. SI checks them for outdated details, gaps, and unclear calls to action. It maps which moments have no message at all. It drafts replacements and new messages for approval.
setup: Copies or screenshots of current system emails. You also need the list of customer journey steps. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: The owner approves every message before it is switched on.
Opt-in and unsubscribe rules are followed.
Changes are tested with a test address first.

examples.scenario: The new-patient welcome email still lists an old address. A replacement is drafted with parking and what to wear.
There is no follow-up after a tour. A short sequence is drafted with a link to book a second visit.
The abandoned-cart email offers a discount the owner no longer gives. A version without it is drafted.

copy_prompt: Here are my automated emails [files or screenshots] and the customer steps [list]. Check each email for outdated details, gaps and unclear calls to action. List steps with no email. Draft replacements and new emails in my voice [example]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: System messages are accurate and match each other. Gaps in the customer journey are filled.

title: Job postings drafted from a quick description of the role
summary: SI turns a manager's rough notes into a clear job posting. The notes describe the role. SI also drafts screening questions. SI drafts a short interview plan.
problem: Job postings get copied from old ones or the internet. Duties are vague. Requirements do not match the actual job. The wrong people apply. The right ones skip it.
what_si_does: SI starts from the manager's notes or a voice memo. It drafts a posting with a plain summary. It lists real day-to-day duties. It lists must-have and nice-to-have requirements. It includes schedule, pay range if you share it, and how to apply. It suggests a few job-related screening questions. It flags wording that could discourage qualified applicants by accident.
setup: Manager notes, past postings, and your standard benefits text. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: The hiring manager approves the posting before it is published.
Requirements are checked to be job-related.
A person confirms pay transparency and posting rules where you hire.

examples.scenario: Notes on a second-year apprentice role become a posting. It states the license stage, truck and tool details, and on-call expectations.
A seasonal tax preparer posting lists software used. It lists busy-season hours and remote options.
A line cook posting lists the stations and shift pattern. It says what a trial shift involves.

copy_prompt: Here are my notes on a [role]: [paste]. Draft a job posting with a short summary, day-to-day duties, must-have and nice-to-have requirements, schedule, pay range [if provided], and how to apply. Suggest [5] job-related screening questions. Flag any wording that could discourage qualified applicants. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Clearer postings that attract better-matched applicants.
caution: Employment and anti-discrimination laws apply. Screening criteria must be job-related. Apply them the same way each time. SI should never score on protected characteristics. Some places regulate hiring tools that run without a person. A person makes every hiring decision.

title: Job application summaries against the role's criteria
summary: SI writes a short digest of each application. It uses the criteria you set for the role. The hiring manager reads that digest and decides.
problem: A posting brings in dozens or hundreds of applications. Busy managers skim. They miss good candidates. They apply different standards on different days.
what_si_does: SI reads each application. It writes a digest against the written, job-related criteria. Criteria include required license or certification. They also include relevant experience, availability, and answers to screening questions. SI notes where information is missing. It groups applications into meets criteria, partly meets, and does not show the requirement. Each group includes the reason. SI does not reject anyone. The manager reviews.
setup: The role's written criteria. Access to applications from the job board or applicant tracker. Setup is often a day or two per role type.
human_checks: A person reviews every application group and makes all decisions.
SI ignores names, photos, ages, and other protected characteristics in its summaries.
Criteria and outcomes are reviewed from time to time so they stay the same and fair.

examples.scenario: SI writes a digest of caregiver applications. It covers certification, driving, and weekend availability. Missing certification dates are noted.
SI writes a digest of journeyman applicants. It covers license status and type of work. The owner calls the ones who meet the requirements.
SI writes a digest of teaching applications. It covers subject certification and grade-level experience. The principal reviews them.

copy_prompt: Here are the written criteria for [role]: [paste]. Summarize each application in [folder/applicant tracker] against those criteria only, ignoring names, photos, age and other personal characteristics. Group them into meets, partly meets and does not show the requirement, with a one-line reason and any missing information. Do not reject anyone. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Managers spend their time on the most relevant applicants. The first read is the same for everyone.
caution: Employment and anti-discrimination laws apply. Screening criteria must be job-related. Apply them the same way each time. SI should never score on protected characteristics. Some places regulate hiring tools that run without a person. A person makes every hiring decision.

title: Interview scheduling and a matching question kit
summary: SI lines up interview times. It works with candidates and interviewers. It prepares a matching question set for each role. It also prepares a scoring sheet.
problem: Interviews take a string of emails to schedule. Each interviewer asks different questions. That makes candidates hard to compare.
what_si_does: SI drafts messages to shortlisted candidates. The messages offer times that work for the interviewers. SI books confirmed slots. It sends reminders. For each role it prepares a short kit. Every candidate gets the same job-related questions. The kit says what a good answer covers. It includes a simple scoring sheet for interviewers to fill in.
setup: Calendar access for interviewers, candidate contacts, and the role's criteria. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: Candidate messages are approved before sending.
The hiring manager approves the questions.
Interview notes and scores are kept with access limited to the hiring team.

examples.scenario: Three hygienist candidates are offered times around the dentist's patient schedule. The kit covers patient communication. It also covers sterilization procedures.
A designer candidate gets times with two interviewers. The kit includes a short portfolio review structure.
Program coordinator interviews use the same questions for all candidates. Board members on the panel use them too.

copy_prompt: For [role], draft messages to these candidates [list] offering [3] times that fit [interviewers' calendars]. Prepare an interview kit with [6] job-related questions, what a strong answer covers, and a scoring sheet. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Less scheduling back-and-forth. Fairer, easier comparisons between candidates.
caution: Employment and anti-discrimination laws apply. Screening criteria must be job-related. Apply them the same way each time. SI should never score on protected characteristics. Some places regulate hiring tools that run without a person. A person makes every hiring decision.

title: A new-hire onboarding checklist that actually gets followed
summary: SI builds an onboarding plan for that role. It sends reminders to whoever owns each step. It tracks what is done.
problem: First weeks are improvised. Accounts are not ready. Paperwork is chased late. Training depends on who has time that day.
what_si_does: SI uses your standard onboarding steps and the role. It builds a dated checklist. The list covers paperwork, accounts and keys, and equipment. It also covers introductions, training sessions, and first-month check-ins. Each step has an owner. SI sends reminders to owners before due dates. It drafts a welcome email with first-day details. It reports what is still open.
setup: Your onboarding steps, role templates, and the tools for tasks and email. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: HR or the manager approves the plan and any messages to the new hire.
Personal documents are handled in your HR system, not in chat or email.
The responsible person confirms required legal paperwork.

examples.scenario: A new leasing agent's plan includes software logins. It includes a ride-along with a senior agent. It includes a fair-housing training session in week one.
A new prep cook gets food-safety training. They get a station walkthrough. Uniform sizing happens before the first shift.
A new paralegal's accounts are scheduled. Conflict-system training is scheduled. A meeting with each practice group is scheduled.

copy_prompt: Using our onboarding steps [paste] and this role [description], build a dated checklist for [name] starting [date], with an owner for each step. Draft a welcome email with first-day details. Set reminders for owners [2] days before each step. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: New hires get a steadier start. Fewer steps are missed.

title: A helper that answers staff questions from your own documents
summary: SI answers staff questions from your own documents. Questions can cover procedures, policies, products, and prices. It says where it found the answer.
problem: Staff interrupt the owner or senior people with the same questions all day. The answers exist in a handbook, price sheet, or old email. Nobody can find them quickly.
what_si_does: SI is connected to an approved set of internal documents. These include the handbook, procedures, price lists, spec sheets, and FAQs. Staff ask in chat. SI answers with a short reply and a link to the source. When the documents do not cover a question, it says so. It routes the question to the right person. The gap is logged so the documents can be updated.
setup: A tidy set of approved documents and a chat tool. Setup is often one to two weeks. Most of that time is organizing the documents.
human_checks: Only approved documents are used. Sources are always shown.
Questions about pay, discipline, or personal matters go to a person.
Document owners review the gap log monthly.

examples.scenario: Counter staff ask which filters fit a given unit. They get the answer with a link to the cross-reference sheet.
Front-desk staff check the procedure for a new patient's insurance verification. They get the steps from the office manual.
Store staff check the holiday return policy. They also check the price-match rules.

copy_prompt: Answer staff questions using only these documents [folder]. Give a short answer and link the source. If the documents do not cover it, say so and suggest who to ask [contacts]. Keep a log of unanswered questions. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer interruptions for senior staff. Documents improve as gaps are found.

title: Tracking staff licenses, certifications and training renewals
summary: SI keeps one staff credential list. It covers licenses, certifications, and required training. The list includes expiry dates. It reminds people well before anything lapses.
problem: Licenses, certifications, and required trainings expire on different dates. A lapse can mean someone cannot work. It can also mean a problem at an inspection or audit.
what_si_does: SI reads certificates and records from a shared folder or HR system. It builds a list of each person's credentials. The list includes issue and expiry dates. It sends reminders to the person and their manager ahead of each expiry. It flags anyone scheduled for work that needs a credential they do not hold.
setup: Copies of certificates or HR records. You also need the list of required credentials per role. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A manager confirms dates against the original documents.
A person makes scheduling decisions about uncertified staff.
Credential records are kept with access limited to managers.

examples.scenario: Electrician licenses, lift certifications, and safety training are tracked. A reminder goes out to renew a lift card before a job that needs it.
CPR and first-aid certifications are tracked for every staff member. Background-check renewals are tracked too.
Nursing licenses are tracked for each caregiver. Required annual trainings are tracked too.

copy_prompt: From these certificates and records [folder], build a list of each person's licenses, certifications and trainings with issue and expiry dates. Compare with required credentials per role [file]. Draft reminders [60] and [14] days before expiry, and flag anyone scheduled for work needing a credential they lack. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer surprise lapses. Fewer scrambles before inspections.

title: Reviewing timesheets and time off before payroll
summary: SI checks timesheets before each payroll run. It checks them against schedules and time-off records. It lists anything that looks wrong. A person fixes those items.
problem: Payroll errors come from missed punches. They also come from unapproved overtime and time off that was never recorded. They are found after the paychecks. That is awkward for everyone.
what_si_does: SI compares timesheets with the schedule. It also checks approved time-off requests and job or project codes. It lists missing punches. It lists unusually long shifts. It lists overtime without approval. It lists time off taken but not recorded. It lists hours coded to the wrong job. It prepares a summary for the payroll person. It does not run payroll. It does not approve hours.
setup: Exports from time tracking, scheduling, and time-off records. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A manager resolves each flagged item with the employee.
A person runs and approves payroll.
Wage-and-hour rules are the owner's or payroll provider's responsibility.

examples.scenario: Two crew members are missing clock-outs on the same day. Overtime on a Saturday job was not approved.
A server's paid sick day was taken but not recorded. A cook's hours exceed the schedule by a full shift.
Hours coded to a closed project are flagged. This happens before they are billed or paid.

copy_prompt: Compare these timesheets [export] with the schedule [export], approved time off [export] and job codes [list] for [pay period]. List missing punches, shifts over [12] hours, unapproved overtime, unrecorded time off and miscoded hours. Prepare a summary for payroll. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer payroll corrections after the fact.
caution: Payroll and wage rules are regulated. SI only flags issues. Payroll decisions and tax filings stay with the owner, payroll provider, or accountant.

title: A first read of contracts for the terms that matter
summary: SI highlights the contract terms that matter. That includes dates, renewal terms, payment terms, and unusual clauses. You know what to ask your lawyer or the other side.
problem: Contracts, leases, and vendor agreements get signed after a skim. Auto-renewals come as surprises later. So do notice periods, liability terms, and penalties.
what_si_does: SI reads the contract. It produces a plain summary. The summary covers parties, term, renewal and notice, and payment terms. It also covers termination, liability and insurance requirements, and exclusivity. It notes anything that differs from your usual terms or a checklist you provide. It lists questions to raise. It does not say whether a clause is acceptable or enforceable.
setup: The contract. Ideally, a checklist of terms you care about, or a standard version to compare against. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: A lawyer reviews anything significant before signing.
SI's summary is checked against the actual text.
SI never signs, accepts, or sends contracts.

examples.scenario: A new commercial lease summary highlights a personal guarantee. It also highlights a percentage-rent clause and the required notice to renew.
A client's master services agreement is compared with the agency's standard terms. It flags an unlimited revision clause and payment at 90 days.
A grant agreement's reporting deadlines and restrictions on spending are pulled into a calendar. They are also pulled into a summary.

copy_prompt: Read this contract [file]. Summarize parties, term, renewal and notice, payment, termination, liability, insurance, exclusivity and any unusual clauses. Compare it with [my checklist or standard terms] and list differences and questions for my lawyer. Do not give a legal opinion. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: You go into contract talks knowing which terms matter. Legal review time goes to the important questions.
caution: This is an organizing aid. It is not legal advice. SI may miss or misread terms. Have a qualified lawyer review contracts that matter.

title: Filling routine forms from saved company details
summary: SI fills vendor setup forms. It also fills applications, permits, and questionnaires. It uses a saved set of company details. It stops before anything is submitted.
problem: The same information is typed into form after form. That includes legal name, tax ID, insurance details, addresses, and contacts. Errors creep in. Forms sit unfinished.
what_si_does: SI keeps a profile of verified company details and documents. These include certificate of insurance, licenses, and standard answers. For each new form, it fills what it can. It lists fields it could not answer. It attaches the right documents. It stops before signing or submitting. It leaves the finished draft for review.
setup: A verified company profile and document folder. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: A person checks and submits every form.
Sensitive identifiers are stored securely and shared only where required.
SI never signs on anyone's behalf.

examples.scenario: A general contractor's subcontractor packet is filled. It includes license numbers, insurance limits, and safety program answers. Two questions are left for the owner.
A grocery distributor's vendor setup form is completed. The food-safety certificate is attached.
Venue permit applications for an outdoor event are pre-filled from the event details.

copy_prompt: Using my company profile [file] and documents [folder], fill out this form [file or link]. List any fields you could not complete and attach the matching documents. Do not sign or submit. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Forms are completed faster. They match each other more often. There are fewer errors.
caution: For tax and government forms, SI fills in information you have already verified. It does not decide tax classifications or legal answers. Confirm anything you are unsure of with your accountant or lawyer.

title: Short briefs from long documents
summary: SI reads long documents and writes a short brief. Sources can be regulations, bid packages, reports, or board packets. The brief says what matters to you and what to do next.
problem: Important documents are long and dense. Reading them carefully takes time nobody has. Key requirements and deadlines get missed.
what_si_does: SI reads the document. It writes a brief. The brief says what it is and the key points. It lists requirements or decisions that affect you. It lists deadlines and open questions. Each point has page references so you can check the source.
setup: The document and a short description of what you care about. Setup is minimal.
human_checks: Important points are checked against the page references.
A qualified person confirms interpretations of rules.
SI flags uncertainty rather than guessing.

examples.scenario: A large bid package becomes a brief. It covers scope, submission deadline, bonding, and insurance requirements. It includes the pre-bid meeting date, with page numbers.
A city's new food-service regulations are summarized. The brief says what changes for kitchens and when it takes effect.
A long board packet becomes a two-page brief. It lists the votes coming up and the questions worth asking.

copy_prompt: Read this document [file]. I am [role] at [organization] and care about [topics]. Write a brief with key points, requirements affecting us, deadlines and open questions, with page references for each. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Long documents get a careful first read quickly. The important parts are easier to find.
caution: The brief is not legal advice. That is true for a regulation, contract, or legal notice. Confirm interpretations with a qualified professional.

title: Drafting bids, RFP responses and grant applications from past answers
summary: SI drafts replies to bids, RFPs, and grants from your past files. It lists what still needs a person to answer.
problem: Each application asks similar questions in new words. Teams rewrite the same answers from scratch. They work under a deadline. They miss required parts.
what_si_does: SI reads the request. It builds a checklist of every required section, attachment, and format rule. It drafts answers from past submissions, capability statements, and project summaries. It marks each answer as reused, adapted, or new. It lists questions with no good source answer. It also makes a submission checklist with the deadline.
setup: A folder of past submissions, capability statements, bios, and project summaries. Setup is often a few days to organize the library.
human_checks: A person reviews every answer and all budget figures.
Claims about past work are checked against records.
A person does the submission.

examples.scenario: SI drafts a foundation grant from last year's proposal and program reports. It flags the new evaluation section as needing input.
A city's request for proposals gets a checklist. SI drafts answers from earlier public-sector bids.
SI assembles a qualifications package. It uses matching project sheets and team resumes.

copy_prompt: Read this request [file]. Build a checklist of required sections, attachments, formats and the deadline. Draft answers using these past submissions and documents [folder], marking each as reused, adapted or new. List questions with no good source. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Applications start from a solid draft. Required parts are less likely to be missed.

title: Pulling data out of PDFs and scans, then filing them
summary: SI reads PDFs, scans, and photos. It pulls the fields you need into a spreadsheet. It also renames and files the documents the same way each time.
problem: Facts sit trapped in PDFs, scans, and phone photos. These include statements, forms, delivery notes, and certificates. Someone retypes them. The files pile up in a messy downloads folder.
what_si_does: SI reads each document. It pulls the fields you name: dates, names, amounts, reference numbers, and line items. It writes them to a spreadsheet with a link to the source file. It renames files with a set pattern. It moves them into the right folders. It lists documents it could not read clearly.
setup: A source folder, the list of fields, and a naming pattern. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: A person spot-checks pulled values against the documents.
Unreadable or uncertain fields are flagged, not guessed.
Original files are kept unchanged.

examples.scenario: A year of scanned utility bills across buildings becomes a sheet. It shows usage and cost by building and month.
SI renames proof-of-delivery scans by load number. It pulls delivery dates for billing.
SI files faxed referral forms by referring practice. It logs key referral details for the scheduling team.

copy_prompt: For each document in [folder], extract [fields] into [sheet] with a link to the file. Rename each file as [pattern] and move it to [folder rules]. List any document or field you could not read clearly. Do not change the original contents. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Less retyping. Documents can actually be found later.
caution: Medical records and other personal data must follow the privacy rules that apply to you. HIPAA is one example. Use approved, secure tools only.

title: Comparing vendors, tools or options in one decision sheet
summary: SI researches options for a purchase or decision. It lays them out side by side against your needs, with sources.
problem: Picking a new supplier, software tool, or service means reading websites, quotes, and reviews. Those sources never compare the same things. Decisions often rest on who had the best sales call.
what_si_does: SI starts from your needs and the options you are looking at. It collects published facts and the quotes you have. It builds a comparison sheet. The sheet covers price, terms, and features against your needs. It also covers contract length, support, and open questions for each vendor. It flags where facts are missing. It flags claims that come only from the vendor.
setup: Your needs and the quotes or vendor names. Setup is minimal.
human_checks: The owner makes the decision.
Facts are linked to sources and checked before relying on them.
Questions for vendors are sent by a person.

examples.scenario: SI compares three practice-management systems. It covers scheduling, how imaging connects, monthly cost, moving data, and contract length.
SI compares quotes for two truck lease offers. It covers mileage limits, upkeep, and ending the lease early.
SI compares three insurance quotes on coverage limits and exclusions. It also lists questions for the broker.

copy_prompt: I need to choose [type of vendor or tool]. My requirements are [list]. Compare these options [names, quotes, links] side by side on price, terms, requirements met, contract length and support. Link sources and flag anything missing or based only on vendor claims. List questions to ask each vendor. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Decisions rest on a clear comparison, not a sales pitch.

title: Handing repeating web-portal chores to SI
summary: SI works through repeating tasks in web portals. It downloads statements, checks status, and enters routine data. It stops before any final step.
problem: Admin work is full of small portal tasks. Download this month's statements from six sites. Check claim or permit status. Update the same info in three places. Each task is quick. Together they eat hours.
what_si_does: With access you grant, SI logs into the portals you list. It follows the written steps for each chore. It downloads files into the right folders. It records statuses in a sheet. It fills routine data entries. It stops before any step that submits, pays, accepts terms, or changes account settings. Then it asks.
setup: A written list of chores and steps. Access is set up the way you choose. Limited-permission user accounts are preferred. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: SI stops before any submit, payment, signature, or setting change.
Access uses limited-permission accounts where possible. Passwords are not shared in chat.
A person spot-checks downloads and entries.

examples.scenario: On the first business day, SI downloads utility and bank statements from each portal. It files them by property.
SI checks insurance claim status in payer portals. It records which claims need follow-up.
SI checks permit status weekly on the town portals for each active job. It logs the status in the job sheet.

copy_prompt: Do these portal chores [list with steps] for [period]. Download files into [folders] with names [pattern], record statuses in [sheet], and enter this routine data [file]. Stop before any step that submits, pays, signs, accepts terms or changes settings. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Routine portal work gets done on schedule. Nobody has to set aside hours for it.

title: A weekly announcements email for members
summary: SI gathers the week's events, schedule changes, and notices. It uses your calendar and notes from contributors. It drafts the members' email for approval.
problem: The weekly email depends on one volunteer or staff member. That person collects items from everyone by text and email. Items arrive late. Details are wrong. The email goes out late or not at all.
what_si_does: SI collects items from a submission form, the shared calendar, and forwarded emails. It checks dates and times against the calendar. It drafts the email in your usual layout. The draft covers this week's schedule, upcoming events, notices, volunteer needs, and celebrations. It lists items with missing details for the editor.
setup: A submission form, calendar access, and a past issue as a template. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: The editor or administrator approves the email before it goes out.
Personal news about illness or a death is included only with permission.
Mailing lists follow subscribe and unsubscribe rules.

examples.scenario: SI pulls service times for the week, a guest speaker, and the kiddush sponsor. It also pulls a volunteer call for the holiday. These go into the Thursday email.
Pool hours, a landscaping schedule, and the next board meeting go into the weekly bulletin.
SI gathers game schedule changes, field closures, and picture-day details from coaches.

copy_prompt: Collect items for [week] from [submission form, calendar, forwarded emails]. Check dates and times against [calendar]. Draft the members' email in this layout [past issue] with schedule, events, notices, volunteer needs and celebrations. List items with missing details. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: The weekly email goes out on time. It has fewer errors. There is less chasing.

title: Donation thank-yous and acknowledgment letters
summary: SI drafts personal thank-you letters and acknowledgment receipts from donation records. It uses wording your accountant has approved.
problem: Thank-yous go out weeks late or not at all. Acknowledgment letters need specific details. Preparing them one by one is slow.
what_si_does: SI reads new donations from your donor system or payment exports. It drafts a thank-you that names the gift and any designation. It prepares an acknowledgment with the details your approved template requires. It flags gifts that need special handling. Those include large gifts, in-kind gifts, or gifts in memory of someone. It also compiles year-end summaries per donor.
setup: Donation records and an acknowledgment template approved by your accountant. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A person reviews and sends every letter.
Acknowledgment wording is approved by the organization's accountant.
Large, in-kind, and memorial gifts are handled personally.

examples.scenario: Gifts from a holiday drive get thank-yous within the week. In-kind food donations are listed by description, not value.
Monthly donors get a short note about the animals adopted that month. Year-end summaries are prepared in January.
Sponsors of a show get a thank-you. It names the production and their program listing.

copy_prompt: For donations in [export] since [date], draft a thank-you for each that mentions the gift and designation, using this tone [example]. Prepare acknowledgments using this approved template [file]. Flag gifts over [amount], in-kind gifts and memorial gifts. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Donors are thanked promptly and accurately.
caution: Tax: acknowledgment rules depend on where you are and the type of gift. Use wording approved by your accountant. SI does not value in-kind gifts. SI does not advise donors on deductions.

title: Volunteer sign-ups, reminders and gap filling
summary: SI organizes volunteer sign-ups and sends reminders. It spots unfilled shifts. It drafts targeted asks to people likely to help.
problem: Volunteer coordination runs on group texts and memory. Shifts go unfilled until the last minute. The same few people get asked every time.
what_si_does: SI keeps the sign-up sheet current from form responses and replies. It sends reminders before each shift. It lists unfilled slots. For gaps, it drafts a short ask. The ask goes to volunteers who have helped with that kind of task before. They have not been asked recently.
setup: A sign-up form or sheet, volunteer contacts, and past participation. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: The coordinator approves messages to volunteers.
Volunteers who opted out are not contacted.
Roles that need background checks are filled only by cleared volunteers.

examples.scenario: Weekday lunch shifts are tracked. A Wednesday gap gets an ask to three people who have done that shift before.
Build-day volunteers get reminders with the site address and what to wear.
Book-fair shifts are filled. Parents get reminders the evening before.

copy_prompt: Using sign-ups [sheet/form] and volunteer history [file], list unfilled shifts for [period]. Draft reminders for confirmed volunteers [1] day before. For each gap, draft a short ask to [3] volunteers who have done similar shifts and have not been asked in [30] days. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer last-minute gaps. The volunteer load is spread more evenly.

title: Event registration, seating and reminders
summary: SI combines registrations and payments. It flags unpaid or duplicate entries. It drafts seating and name tags. It sends approved reminders.
problem: Event logistics live in several places. There is a form, a payment tool, a spreadsheet, and someone's notes. The last week before the event is frantic. Details slip.
what_si_does: SI merges registrations and payments. It lists unpaid and duplicate entries. It produces headcounts, dietary lists, and name tags. It drafts seating by your rules. Households sit together. Sponsors sit near the front. It drafts reminder and logistics emails. It produces the final count for the caterer or venue.
setup: Registration and payment exports, seating rules, and message templates. Setup is often a few days before the event.
human_checks: The organizer approves seating and every message.
Payment follow-ups are sent by a person.
Final counts to the caterer or venue are confirmed by a person.

examples.scenario: SI matches the annual dinner's registrations with payments. Members who registered twice through two links are merged.
SI drafts foursomes for a charity golf outing. It lists sponsor signage.
SI produces a reunion's dietary list and name tags. Reminders go out three days before, after approval.

copy_prompt: Combine these registrations [file] and payments [file] for [event]. List unpaid and duplicate entries, draft seating for [tables] tables of [10] using these rules [paste], and produce dietary and name-tag lists. Draft a reminder email for [3] days before. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Event logistics are calmer in the final week. Fewer details slip.

title: Membership renewals and a clean member list
summary: SI tracks renewal dates and drafts reminders. It cleans up the member list. It merges duplicates and flags outdated contact details.
problem: Renewals depend on someone remembering to send reminders. The member list has duplicates, old emails, and households listed three ways.
what_si_does: SI reads the member list and payment records. It lists members due to renew or lapsed. It drafts reminders in a friendly sequence. It proposes cleanup. That includes merging duplicates, flagging bounced emails, and making names and households consistent. Lapsed members who were active get a personal-style note. A board member can send it.
setup: Member list and payment exports, and your renewal schedule. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: Merges and deletions are confirmed by a person.
Reminders are approved before sending.
Members with hardship arrangements are handled personally.

examples.scenario: Families due to renew in March get reminders. Households listed under two parents' names are merged.
Lapsed member companies are listed with their last event attended. A board member can call them.
Bounced email addresses are flagged ahead of the spring renewal mailing.

copy_prompt: Using the member list [file] and payments [file], list members due to renew in [period] and those lapsed. Draft a reminder sequence [timing]. Propose merges for likely duplicates, flag bounced or missing emails, and standardize household names. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: More renewals happen on time. The member list is one you can trust.

title: Session notes into progress updates for families or clients
summary: After each session or class, SI uses the instructor's quick notes. It writes a short, consistent progress update. A parent or client can then receive it.
problem: Instructors and coaches jot notes. They rarely have time to write updates. Families or clients hear little until there is a problem. The updates that do go out vary a lot.
what_si_does: SI takes the instructor's notes or voice memo. It writes a short update in a consistent format. The update names what was taught and what went well. It also names what to practice and what comes next. It keeps a running record per learner so trends are visible. It flags notes that suggest a concern. The instructor handles those personally.
setup: A simple notes form or voice memo path, a template, and contacts. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: The instructor approves each update before it is sent.
Concerns are communicated personally, not by template.
Notes about minors are stored with limited access.

examples.scenario: A math tutor's two-line note becomes a parent update. It covers fractions practice and next week's focus.
Lesson notes become a weekly message. It lists the pieces to practice and a tip for the tricky passage.
Each lesson produces a short summary of skills covered. It also lists what to practice before the road test.

copy_prompt: Turn these session notes [paste] for [learner] into a short update for [parent/client] with what was covered, what went well, what to practice and what is next, using this template [example]. Flag any note that suggests a concern. Add it to the running record [file]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Families and clients stay informed. Instructors spend less time writing.
caution: If sessions are therapy, counseling, or medical, the notes are protected health information. Use tools that meet your privacy rules. A clinician must review them.

title: Lesson plans, quizzes and training materials for instructors
summary: SI drafts lesson plans, quizzes, handouts, and first-pass feedback. It uses your curriculum or materials. The instructor reviews and adapts them.
problem: Instructors, trainers, and teachers spend evenings building plans and quizzes from scratch. Feedback on written work is slow. There is so much of it.
what_si_does: SI starts from your curriculum, textbook pages, or training manual. It drafts a lesson or session plan. The plan has goals, activities, timing, and a short check for understanding. It creates quizzes at different levels with answer keys. It drafts first-pass feedback on written work against a rubric. The instructor edits that feedback.
setup: The source materials, a rubric if relevant, and examples of the format you use. Setup is minimal.
human_checks: The instructor reviews every plan, quiz, and piece of feedback.
Grades are assigned by the instructor, not SI.
Student work is handled under the program's privacy policy.

examples.scenario: A volunteer tutor gets a session plan and a short reading check. Both are built around a job-application form.
A forklift-safety manual becomes a session outline. SI also drafts a quiz for new warehouse workers.
A science unit gets a lab plan and two quiz versions. SI also drafts feedback on lab reports against the rubric.

copy_prompt: Using these materials [files] and this format [example], draft a [length] session plan for [audience] with goals, activities, timing and a check for understanding. Create a [10]-question quiz with an answer key at [level]. Draft feedback on these submissions [files] against this rubric [file]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Prep takes less of the instructor's own time. Feedback gets back to learners sooner.

title: Board packets and minutes for volunteer boards
summary: SI assembles the board packet from committee reports and financials. It drafts the agenda. It turns meeting notes into draft minutes for the secretary.
problem: Volunteer boards run on late reports. The packet is assembled the night before. Minutes are written weeks later from memory.
what_si_does: SI collects committee reports, the treasurer's summary, and any proposals from a shared folder. It flags what is missing. It assembles a packet with an agenda. It also writes a one-page summary of decisions needed. After the meeting, it drafts minutes from notes or a transcript. The draft lists motions, votes, and action items.
setup: A shared folder, a past packet, and minutes as templates. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: The chair approves the agenda and packet.
The secretary reviews and finalizes the minutes before approval by the board.
Confidential matters are handled outside the shared packet.

examples.scenario: The packet includes the manager's report, a roof bid comparison, and the reserve fund summary. A note says the landscaping committee report is missing.
Minutes from the monthly meeting list the vote on new member-owner discounts. They also list the follow-up tasks.
The fall packet includes the fundraiser results and the budget for the spring events.

copy_prompt: Gather reports from [folder] for the [date] board meeting. List what is missing, draft an agenda using [past agenda], and write a one-page summary of decisions needed. After the meeting, draft minutes from these notes [paste] with motions, votes and action items. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Board members arrive prepared. Minutes are ready while the meeting is still fresh.
caution: Minutes can be legal records for some organizations. The secretary and board should approve the final version. Recording requires participants' consent.

title: Moving off a retired inventory app without losing your reorder history
summary: When the inventory or purchase-order tool shuts down, SI reads the export and rebuilds suppliers, past orders, and reorder rules into a sheet you can use next week.
problem: The app you used for stock and purchase orders is gone. What you have left is an export. Supplier names, past orders, and reorder rules sit in those files. They are not a Monday list of what to buy. A working reorder list and a low-stock watch assume the system is still running. This job is the move itself.
what_si_does: SI reads the export (CSV or spreadsheet). It lists suppliers, items, past purchase orders, and quantities. It also lists any reorder points or par levels that are actually in the file. It maps those into a simple sheet. You see who you buy from, what you last ordered, and a suggested reorder line you can edit. It flags fields the export does not contain, duplicate item names, and suppliers with no contact. It does not place orders. A common version is a Shopify store that exported Stocky before that app shut down. Now it has CSVs instead of a weekly system. The same steps apply to any retired inventory or purchase-order tool that left you a file.
setup: You need the export folder. Add a note on which columns matter (supplier, SKU, on hand, last cost, reorder point). Add one recent order you still trust as a sample. human_checks: A person confirms the mapping before anyone orders from it.

title: Abandoned-checkout follow-up drafts from your store records
summary: SI lists checkouts that were started and not finished. It drafts a short follow-up from the actual cart. You send only if the customer is allowed to hear from you.
problem: People start checkout and leave. Follow-up never happens, or a generic automated email goes out with a discount you no longer offer. what_si_does: On a schedule you choose, SI reads abandoned checkouts from the store or an export. It lists ones still incomplete after a wait you set, with the items, total, and when the checkout was left. It drops checkouts that later became orders, checkouts with no email, and anyone on your do-not-contact list. It drafts a short follow-up from your past replies and policy. setup: You need read access or an export of checkouts and completed orders. Add your contact rules (who may be emailed, how long to wait) and a few follow-ups you actually sent. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A person approves every message. SI never sends.

Discounts and stock claims come only from what you provided.
